overview:
California's 31st District sits about eight points to the left of the country, and Democratic incumbent Gil Cisneros is running for re-election. The general election matches him against Republican Eric Ching, who advanced to the ballot alongside the incumbent.

The available evidence points firmly toward Cisneros. He has raised roughly $705,000 to Ching's $82,000 and holds a wide cash advantage, while outside spending in the race has been negligible. No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and an environment favoring Democrats. Prediction markets price Cisneros around a 96 percent favorite. With no polling suggesting competition and the challenger showing little financial traction, the seat rates as Safe Democratic, though the absence of survey data leaves some room for surprise.
